title: Acceptance criteria for streaming-envelope reconciliation and tool-call observability
creator: Maya Patel
description: Define explicit, testable acceptance criteria for streaming structured outputs (progressive JSON/envelope emissions) when invoking external tools or functions. This ticket covers schema markers, partial-object reconciliation, error classification, replay/idempotency guarantees, backpressure signals, and telemetry keys required to link stream fragments and tool invocations for debugging and SLO calculations.
background: Multiple PM tickets and design drafts surfaced ambiguity in how partial/streamed JSON should be treated when tool calls are in-flight or when generators emit progressive fields. Engineering has implemented a streaming envelope prototype but telemetry does not reliably tie emitted fragments to downstream tool requests. We need acceptance criteria that the runtime, API, and console can use for QA, rollout gating, and SLA commitments.
scope_changes: This ticket narrows prior broad 'streaming schema' work to three concrete areas: 1) stream envelope markers and reconciliation rules, 2) deterministic idempotency and retry semantics for tool calls triggered from streams, 3) telemetry/traceable identifiers that join fragments and tool-side outcomes. Excludes: prompt-level orchestration UI work, SDK ergonomics refinements (handled separately).
acceptance_criteria: Stream envelope format: The runtime must emit a well-formed top-level envelope for streamed structured outputs: {"envelope_version":"1", "stream_id": <uuid>, "fragment_index": <int>, "payload": <partial_object_or_patch>, "final": <true|false>, "schema_version": <semver>} and the API must accept and persist these fields verbatim. Any deviation fails validation in QA.

Fragment reconciliation: When final=true is received the platform must be able to produce a deterministic final object by applying fragments in fragment_index order using 'last-writer-wins' for scalar fields and array-append semantics for arrays unless payload includes an explicit 'replace' op. QA will test with interleaved fragments and random reordering to validate idempotent reconstruction.

Tool invocation correlation: Each tool/function call triggered during a stream must include the stream_id and the triggering fragment_index in the tool-call request envelope. Telemetry must store both stream_id and fragment_index alongside the tool-call ID so console traces can join generator fragments -> tool request -> tool response.

Partial emission visibility: Console must show partial objects as they arrive (non-blocking) and mark stale fragments (if a fragment is superseded by a later fragment) while still preserving the original fragment history for investigation. Default UI should show live-reconciled view and a 'show history' toggle.

Backpressure and flow-control: The runtime must expose an explicit backpressure signal in the stream envelope (e.g., "flow_hint": "slow_down" or "ok") within 500ms of detecting queue growth beyond the latency SLO threshold. SDKs must surface this as an event for client-side adaption. Tests will simulate traffic bursts to verify signal latency.

Error classification and recovery: Tool-call errors must be classified as transient (retryable), permanent (do not retry), or partial-failure (tool succeeded but returned malformed payload). The platform must provide a deterministic fallback policy: retry up to N with exponential backoff for transient; record and bubble permanent errors to client with a standard error code set. Acceptance tests include injected error modes from mock tool endpoints.

Idempotency and replay: Tool-calls generated from fragments must be idempotent or carry an idempotency key composed of stream_id + fragment_index + tool_action. On retry or reconnection, duplicate tool-calls must not cause duplicate side-effects. QA will run replay scenarios across service restarts to validate idempotency enforcement.

Partial-to-final reconciliation guarantees: In the presence of partial emissions followed by a final emission that changes previously emitted keys, the final object returned by the API must reflect final=true state; consoles and APIs must expose both final object and patch delta history for audits. Test vectors should include key-removal, key-rewrite, and array reordering cases.

Telemetry and trace sampling: Every stream must emit an initial trace event with stream_id, model_id, model_config_id, client_region, and route_id. Tool-call traces must include the parent trace id and fragment index. Sampling policy must ensure at least 1% of streams are fully traced end-to-end; critical customers (enterprise tier) have configurable 100% tracing. Acceptance verifies trace linkage in the console and log storage indexes.

SLOs and observability metrics: For streamed tool-invocations, the platform must provide metrics: fragments_per_stream, avg_reconstruction_latency(ms), tool-call_latency(ms), tool-call_success_rate(%), idempotent_replay_count. Dashboards must render these metrics by route and model. QA will validate metric presence with synthetic load.

Compatibility & migration: The runtime must continue to accept legacy single-json streaming (no envelope) for a deprecation period of 3 months. When legacy is used, system must synthesize stream_id and fragment_index to enable telemetry linkage. Test ensures both formats are accepted during migration window.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope validator that fail on missing envelope_version, missing stream_id, or non-integer fragment_index.
Integration test: spawn generator that emits 10 out-of-order fragments then final=true; assert reconstructed final object equals expected and fragments logged with correct fragment_index.
Fault-injection: mock tool returns 500 on first two calls, then 200; assert retry/backoff policy observed and single final side-effect recorded (idempotency key validated).
Telemetry test: create stream and tool calls, then query traces in console; assert joins exist and sampling thresholds respected.
Backpressure test: simulate 3x traffic over SLO; confirm flow_hint appears within 500ms and SDK surfaces event.
Migration test: send legacy single-json stream and assert synthesised stream metadata present in telemetry and reconstructed object consistent.
rollback_plan: If runtime changes cause regressions in production streaming behavior or telemetry linkage, rollback to prior runtime image and disable envelope enforcement via a runtime feature flag. Notify customers with open streams to reconnect; run migration compatibility shim to synthesize missing fields.
tradeoffs: Choosing a stricter envelope format improves observability and deterministic reconciliation but increases payload size and requires SDK updates. We will accept a small payload overhead to gain end-to-end traceability. Full locking semantics for conflicting fragments were rejected due to complexity and latency impact; we adopt last-writer-wins + ops in payload instead.
open_questions: What is the maximum allowed size for an individual fragment payload? (affects memory/ingress limits)
Should we support alternative reconciliation strategies per-route (e.g., CRDTs) or keep single global policy?
Do we want a separate 'tool_call_outcome' field within fragments to allow generator-runner co-located tool post-processing to annotate streams?
